title: About thirteen tunes without credit, including 'Rocking in Rhythm'
summary: He says he has about thirteen uncredited tunes in the discography, including 'Saturday Night Function', and that Duke put Carney's name on 'Rocking in Rhythm' though Carney could not compose.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: You told me about 'Mood Indigo', that -- did he take any other music of yours that you didn't get credit for?
Oh, I got about 13 tunes. You'll see them on that thing I gave you --
-- to look at. Yeah, that discog -- whatever you -- what do you call it?
Yeah, discography. You'll see my name on them. I never did get credit for it. I had about 13.
And these are all things that Duke put his name on
'Saturday Night Function', Check and Doublecheck' -- not 'Check and Doublecheck' 'Rocking in Rhythm' -- he put Harry's name on there.
And you said Harry didn't make any contribution?

Nothing, he couldn't compose a note. He didn't know nothing. Harry couldn't compose nothing if he tried, God bless his soul. He's a good boy, but he couldn't compose nothing. Well, he did that because Harry was riding him around.
